patch.value: GH-1662: an infeasible --token-budget on context --for orient exits 0 with no context and contradictory receipts, its restore_with retry fails, and get/list intent receipts undercount the emitted envelope

GitHub issue #1662 (reported 2026-11-04 against 2026.11.4 from an agent-UX audit). Reproduced 2026-11-05 on the installed 2026.11.4 CLI in a disposable sandbox tracker holding one claimed Task with a linked file, doc and test. (1) pm context --for orient --token-budget 600 --json exits 0 with no context. The envelope (1,421 B, about 356 tokens) carries budget_exceeded with omitted_result true and reason effective_budget_infeasible, and context_intent says within_budget false and result_omitted true, yet read_output in the same envelope says within_budget true and result_omitted false. The same value spelled canonically, --output-budget 600, exits 2 with output_budget_exceeded, so the compatibility alias and the canonical flag disagree on success. The reporter reproduced the contradiction through the SDK with client.context({for: 'orient', tokenBudget: '600'}). (2) The advertised restore_with, pm context --for orient --token-budget 700 --limit 1, exits 2 with output_budget_exceeded (744 B), so following the envelope's own recovery is a retry that still yields no context. (3) pm get <id> --for inspect --token-budget 500 --json emits 2,149 B (about 538 tokens) while context_intent claims estimated_tokens 385 and within_budget true, and pm list --for triage --token-budget 500 --limit 2 --json emits 2,115 B (about 529 tokens) while claiming 376. Both exceed the budget they report fitting, because the intent receipt and the surrounding envelope are not part of the estimate. Expected: one budget contract for canonical and legacy spellings, an omitted required result is unambiguously unsuccessful (non-zero exit, every receipt agrees), the estimate covers the complete serialized envelope including receipts, and a suggested retry is verified against the same estimator. Why it matters for agents: a shell agent proceeds after exit 0 with no project context, an SDK consumer reading the shared read_output receipt reaches the same wrong conclusion, and the supplied recovery spends another call for nothing. This escapes closed acceptance criteria in the same family: pm-yekkvt AC3 (a response that omits its result never reports within_budget true), pm-3crymx AC3 (recovery guidance is verified to work on the corpus that produced the refusal), pm-xam9bt AC4 and AC7 (recovery bindings are executed for legacy budgets and repeated recovery makes progress without cycles), pm-8kzfc4 AC4 (canonical alias migration stays equivalent independently of token limits) and pm-7hbfch AC3 (the envelope carries a measured estimate so a consumer can detect an overrun without measuring bytes). Duplicate check: searched intent budget, receipt, omitted result, restore_with, legacy alias and estimator terms across all statuses, and no open item owns this. The report excludes GH-1428, GH-1552 and GH-1361 as separate subjects.

pm context --for orient with a budget below its smallest feasible projection exits non-zero whether the budget is spelled --token-budget or --output-budget, in CLI, SDK and MCP, and every receipt in the envelope (budget_exceeded, context_intent and read_output) reports result_omitted true and within_budget false; The canonical --output-budget and the legacy --token-budget alias produce the same success, omission and exit status for the same value on the same corpus, proven by a spec that runs both spellings in JSON and TOON; Every restore_with or suggested retry an omission emits is executed by a spec against the same corpus and estimator and returns the requested result, or the envelope names an honest non-numeric alternative instead of a budget that cannot fit; The estimated_tokens that context_intent and read_output report for get --for inspect and list --for triage is computed over the complete serialized envelope including the receipts, and a spec asserts it is at least ceil(emitted UTF-8 bytes / 4) and that within_budget is false whenever the emitted output exceeds the budget; Negative control: reintroducing the intent-only estimate, or exit 0 on an omitted orient result, fails the specs above

In a fresh tracker with one claimed Task: pm context --for orient --token-budget 600 --json (exit 0, no context, contradictory receipts). pm context --for orient --output-budget 600 --json (exit 2). Run the emitted restore_with with --json (exit 2). pm get <id> --for inspect --token-budget 500 --json and pm list --for triage --token-budget 500 --limit 2 --json (receipt estimate below the emitted size)

An omitted required result is unsuccessful on every transport and all receipts agree, canonical and legacy budgets behave identically, suggested retries work, and reported estimates cover the full emitted envelope

message: Triage GitHub issue #1662 into the tracker

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Root causes, reproduced on main af6fd5583 in a sandbox tracker with one claimed Task: (1) the intent estimate measured compact JSON of the projection whatever the delivered encoding, including a row_contract the host strips unless --output-row-contract is requested; pretty JSON was undercounted (get 381 vs 534 emitted, list 375 vs 528) and TOON overcounted, so --token-budget 600 omitted in TOON where --output-budget 600 succeeded. (2) A numeric --output-budget never bound the intent budget, so legacy derived a 1-row limit while canonical kept the declared 3000 ceiling (500 TOON: legacy exit 0, canonical exit 2; 5000 JSON: 988 vs 883 tokens). (3) An omitted intent result (budget_exceeded) never set the exit code, and the read_output receipt attached to it said within_budget true and result_omitted false. (4) restore_with used ceil(estimate/100)*100, so the retry sat at the edge of its own budget. Fix: updateContextIntentEstimate measures through estimateReadOutputTokens in the delivered encoding (the CLI's delivered renderer) and excludes an unrequested row_contract; a numeric canonical --output-budget becomes the intent's effective budget (row derivation, compaction, echo) through both SDK options and the CLI global flag, a canonical omission keeps the shared output_budget_exceeded branch, and --output-budget unbounded never omits; read_output inherits result_omitted from an omitted intent; the CLI exits 2 on isReadResultOmittedForBudget (new SDK export covering both branches); restore_with uses resolveReadOutputRecoveryBudget's 25% margin. Measured after the fix on the same corpus: for 300/500/600/900/1000/3000/5000 in JSON and TOON both spellings give identical exit codes and token counts; the emitted restore_with (pm context --for orient --token-budget 1100 --limit 1) exits 0 with the result. SDK and MCP at 300: every receipt reports result_omitted true; MCP keeps isError unset for budget omissions, as it already does for the canonical refusal.

value.text: Calibration review: measuring the intent in the delivered encoding moved scripts/release/context-intent-calibration.json at the 2,243-item tier only. list delivers 69 rows in 3,162 tokens (was 67 in 3,080) against its 3,200 declaration, next 9 rows in 1,136 (was 8 in 1,053) against 1,200, search 28 rows in 1,766 (was 27 in 1,716) against 1,800. The session orientation sees 111 items in 9,945 of 20,000 tokens (was 107 in 9,687), and the list/search cursor walks need one and three fewer pages. Every intent still fits its declared ceiling; the compact-JSON estimate had been trimming rows the delivered TOON had room for. Approved with pnpm context:intent:calibrate --update.

value.text: Codex batch review round 2 (P2), confirmed and fixed. Measuring the delivered encoding (and, under GH-1678, a custom renderer) removed the convergence guarantee the compact-JSON-only intent estimate had. A deterministic renderer that prints a remainder derived from context_intent.estimated_tokens makes the fixpoint in updateContextIntentEstimate alternate between 200 and 201 forever, so formatOutput never returned. The loop is now bounded by the shared MAX_ESTIMATE_ITERATIONS (8, the same bound the read_output receipt uses). On non-convergence it falls back to the largest estimate observed, so an oscillating receipt never understates within its cycle. Regression: delivered-output-budget.spec.ts 'terminates an intent estimate that a renderer makes oscillate' returns, with estimated_tokens >= the delivered tokens. Negative control: with the unbounded for(;;) loop restored the spec hangs until the 60 s harness timeout (exit 124). Converging inputs are unaffected; the calibration gate is unchanged.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex batch review round 4 (P2), confirmed. The fix covers a wider defect than reported. attachReadOutputContracts settled receipts over the final envelope only on the suppressed-row-contract path. With --output-row-contract requested (or for results without a row_contract key) the intent receipt kept its pre-envelope estimate: 278 tokens for a 412-token delivery. A stable custom renderer was then needlessly sent through the round-3 native fallback. The intent decision itself also ignored the read_output receipt and the requested row contract, so the legacy spelling delivered over its budget with exit 0. Probe: list --for triage --token-budget 400 --output-row-contract delivered 445 tokens, while --output-budget 400 omitted with exit 2; get --for inspect at 700 delivered 705. Fix (src/sdk/context-intent-contracts.ts): attachReadOutputContracts is split into finalizeReadOutputEnvelope, which settles every intent result's receipts over the delivered envelope on every path, and settledIntentOmission. When a delivered, non-unbounded intent read's settled envelope exceeds its intent budget, settledIntentOmission decides it again through intentBudgetOutcome: the legacy budget_exceeded branch with a restore_with from the settled size, or the canonical output_budget_exceeded branch. The omission passes through the read-output stage again, so every receipt agrees and the CLI exits 2. Re-probe: no read under either spelling delivers over its budget. The one remaining boundary difference (get --output-row-contract at 700: legacy omits at 705, canonical fits at 692) is the legacy receipt's migration-hint bytes; docs/READ_OUTPUT_CONTRACTS.md now says so. Regressions in delivered-output-budget.spec.ts: settled native and stable-custom intent receipts with row contracts, the legacy and canonical omission at 400, the named retry budget returning the result, and unbounded keeping its result. Negative control: with the recheck disabled the legacy read exits 0 (expected undefined to be 2).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Round 4 follow-up: omitting a settled over-budget intent read was too harsh. In the calibration gate's 2,243-item session orientation, the read_session and read_output receipts pushed list, search and next past their per-call intent budgets, and those reads had been delivered over budget while claiming within_budget: true. The omission removed them entirely, so later reads suppressed nothing ('orientation session did not suppress repeated item facts'). The recheck is now a second pass instead. settledIntentOverhead measures how far the settled envelope exceeds the intent estimate. attachContextIntentReceipt then charges that overhead against its fit ceiling (keyed through a WeakMap on the second pass's options, invisible to callers), so row and recursive compaction leave room for the receipts. The receipt still reports the caller's budget. A read is omitted only when even its smallest projection cannot fit, and the legacy restore_with then sizes its retry from the complete envelope (intent estimate + overhead). Re-probe: list and get, with and without --output-row-contract, at 300/400/500/700 give identical exit codes and outcomes under --token-budget and --output-budget, and none delivers over budget. The calibration report was re-approved. The only change is the 2,243-tier session_orientation: spent 9,945 -> 8,210 tokens, seen items 111 -> 83, delivered bytes 39,771 -> 32,834, suppressed repeats unchanged at 8. Each session read now fits its own intent budget over its complete envelope.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex batch review round 5: two P2s, both confirmed and fixed. (1) Include projection erased intent refusals. 'pm get <id> --for inspect --output-budget 300 --output-include item --json' returned item: {} with exit 0, because applyIncludeProjection treated output_budget_exceeded and context_intent as unselected sections, so read_output and isReadResultOmittedForBudget reported success. projectReadOutputRows now shapes only results that are not budget omissions (includeProjectionApplies in src/sdk/read-output-contracts.ts). Regression: the integration spec runs that exact CLI invocation from source and expects exit 2 with an omission. Negative control: without the guard it fails. (2) Reserving the measured overhead did not guarantee the re-settled second pass fits. A structured output_format service for next --for execute --token-budget 344 --output-row-contract delivered 345 tokens with exit 0. attachReadOutputContracts now rechecks the re-settled envelope (settledIntentOverBudget). A read still over its intent budget is omitted through intentBudgetOutcome, with restore_with sized from the settled envelope, and that omission passes through the read-output stage. Regression: a budget sweep 300..460 asserts that every read either fits its budget or is omitted with exit 2. Negative control: without the recheck it fails at 'budget 344: expected 345 to be less than or equal to 344'. docs/READ_OUTPUT_CONTRACTS.md states both rules.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex batch review round 6: four P2s, all fixed (src/sdk/context-intent-contracts.ts, src/sdk/read-output-contracts.ts). (1) A successful --output-include projection removed context_intent, so both settled-budget checks were bypassed: 'get --for inspect --fields id,title,description,children --output-include item --token-budget 350 --output-row-contract' delivered 413 tokens with exit 0. settledIntentOverBudget now falls back to the first-pass intent receipt and measures the delivered envelope itself. Negative control: without the fallback the budget sweep fails. (2) collapseContinuationMetadata removed the intent receipt from refused continuation pages, so output_budget_exceeded shipped beside read_output.result_omitted false. An omission is no longer collapsed, and the read_output receipt recognizes either omission discriminator (isReadResultOmittedForBudget). (3) The legacy restore_with dropped --fields, so its retry requested far more data than the named budget allowed and refused again. buildContextIntentRecoveryCommand now carries the caller's --fields. Negative control: without it the executed retry fails. (4) Flipping within_budget after stabilization added an unmeasured byte, so the session under-charged by 1. reconcileIntentFit now runs inside the stabilization loop, so the flag settles with the estimates. With the TT fixture the intent stage already reports within_budget false, so the reorder is a structural guarantee: the exact-charge assertion (560 delivered, 560 estimated, next_state 575 = 15 + 560) holds. Regression: tests/integration/read-output/delivered-output-budget.integration.spec.ts 'binds include-shaped reads, keeps resumed refusals whole, names working retries and charges sessions exactly'. Convergence note: rounds 1-6 found 1, 2, 3, 1, 2 and 4 P2s. Each round mostly found compositions created by the previous round's guards.

value.text: Static-gate findings on the final tree, fixed. (1) scripts/release/token-budget-gate.mjs ran its infeasible-intent negative control ('list --for triage --token-budget 256 --json') through runCliJson, which treats any non-zero exit as a crash. This batch makes an omitted intent result exit 2, so the gate died before reading the receipt. The control now runs with allowFailure, reads the receipt from the failed run, and additionally requires exit_status 2. The spec mock returns 2 for that read, and a new case fails when an omission exits 0. (2) Round 4's settling had started re-estimating omission envelopes, so an omitted result's context_intent.estimated_tokens reported the refusal's own size (203) instead of the omitted result's size (> 256). The receipt then said within_budget false at 203 <= 256. stabilizeSuppressedRowContractReceipts no longer re-estimates the intent receipt of an omitted result; the read_output receipt already measures the delivered envelope exactly. Token budget gate: passed (32 surfaces; infeasible effective intent receipt verified). Calibration gate: passed.

patch.value: Integration specs: spelling matrix 300/600/900/3000 in JSON and TOON; an executed restore_with returning the result; get/list estimates at or above the emitted size; a shaped get refusal exiting 2; agreeing continuation refusals; an exact session charge. Unit sweeps assert fit-or-exit-2. Calibration re-approved (session orientation 9,945 -> 8,210 tokens); token-budget gate requires exit 2 for the infeasible control; agent-task baseline +1 token
Both budget spellings give the same outcome on the same corpus, an omitted result exits 2 with agreeing receipts, restore_with succeeds when executed, and intent receipts cover the emitted envelope

Intent reads now have one budget contract. The intent estimate measures the delivered encoding, without an unrequested row_contract, and is settled over the complete envelope including the read_output receipt. A numeric --output-budget binds the intent budget exactly like --token-budget, in both the SDK and the CLI global flag. A settled envelope over its intent budget is decided again with the measured overhead charged, and is omitted only when it still cannot fit. Every omitted result exits 2, and context_intent, read_output and the omission branch all agree. --output-include and continuation pages never strip a refusal. The legacy restore_with carries the 25% recovery margin and the caller's --fields, so the retry it names returns the result. The new SDK export isReadResultOmittedForBudget detects both branches.
Intent reads obey one budget contract over the bytes they deliver, and every omission is unsuccessful

value.text: Codex review round 7 on PR 1681 (P2, an ordinary caller), confirmed and fixed. 'pm get <id> --fields id,title --for inspect --token-budget 300 --output-row-contract --json' exited 2, but its intent receipt reported 205-210 tokens against a 300-token budget. The settled second pass reserved envelopeOverhead to decide fit, then restored the public budget without adding that overhead to the omitted result's estimate, and stabilization deliberately leaves omitted estimates alone. attachContextIntentReceipt now adds the reserved overhead to an omitted result's estimate, so the published omission explains itself (estimate > budget). Regression: the integration spec runs that exact invocation. Negative control: without the fix it fails with 'expected 205 to be greater than 300'. Token-budget, calibration and agent-task gates pass unchanged.

value.text: Greptile review on PR 1681 (4/5). Finding 2 duplicates Codex round 7 and was fixed in the previous commit. Finding 1 was confirmed and fixed: a canonical intent refusal built by intentBudgetOutcome has no read_output receipt, and with no session, row contract or include selection, applyReadOutputDimensions' canReturnReadOutputUnchanged returned it before attaching one. isReadOutputBudgetExceeded still typed it as PmReadOutputBudgetExceeded, which promises read_output, so SDK callers reading read_output.estimated_tokens threw. canReturnReadOutputUnchanged now never short-circuits a budget omission. Regression: the integration spec scans SDK get --for inspect budgets to the first refusal and reads its read_output estimate. Negative control: without the guard it throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading estimated_tokens)'. Token-budget, calibration and agent-task gates and the SDK surface and contract snapshots pass unchanged.

value.text: CodeRabbit full review of PR 1681 (12 Minor/Trivial). Four quick, realistic findings are fixed in this PR, each with a regression: (a) the TOON complete-receipt one-liner now compares by value, so a receipt with reordered fields still renders 'omission_receipt: complete', and one with an extra field stays verbose; (b) an explicit --output-budget unbounded intent read skips both intent compaction steps, so 'get --for inspect --output-budget unbounded' no longer truncates the body to 240 characters (negative control: the 20,000-character body came back truncated); (c) declaration_feasible is recomputed after a second-pass omission adds its envelope overhead; (d) the restore_with and second-pass omission assertions are now unconditional. The other eight are deferred to new or existing items with typed edges: direct-render and service paths in pm-tgw0ir; include-before-omission, cursor replay and the direct-helper receipt in pm-9gtqgu; nested TOON empties in pm-fkhdy8; Windows recovery quoting as an extension of the existing pm-kjoudp. attachContextIntentReceipt's compaction moved into compactIntentProjection and estimatedIntentProjection to stay under the complexity ceiling.
